question: What is the primary hypothesis regarding the cause of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)?
answer: PCOS is hypothesized to result from functional ovarian hyperandrogenism (FOH) due to dysregulation of androgen secretion, with studies supporting this idea since the initial hypothesis proposed between 1989 and 1995. Two-thirds of PCOS cases exhibit typical FOH, characterized by hyperresponsiveness to gonadotropin stimulation
source: The Pathogenesis of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) - PMC.
